answer: At the computational summit of network participation, proof-of-work systems require each agent to solve cryptographic puzzles that carve a ridge of computational expense across the landscape of identity. The willow-branch growth of network nodes is constrained by the substantial energy and hardware costs each new identity must expend. An attacker attempting to flood the network with fake identities would face exponential resource requirements, as each Sybil node must independently climb the same technical ridge, making large-scale deception economically prohibitive.
